findings.oracle: Real loopback asyncio server on an ephemeral port + a real GuestAgentClient driven through production QEMUSandbox._ensure_agent_connected (no patches). Oracle = the server's own accepted-peer counter and the agent's is_connected flag. Asserts agent.is_connected is True and the server accepted exactly one socket; a companion test reserves-then-releases a dead port and asserts pytest.raises(SandboxError). If production stopped awaiting connect, is_connected stays False and both go red.

Real _poll_for_result driven over real result files. Oracle = the documented contract (stripped all-digit body = decimal exit code, everything else = -1 sentinel), independently asserted: parametrized well-formed cases (0,1,42,255,'007'->7,'  13  '->13), parametrized malformed cases ('','abc','0x42','-1','1.5','exit: 0','42 43')->-1, and a multi-line 'garbage\n7'->-1 pinning whole-file-strip. Asserts exact 3-tuple incl. empty stdout/stderr without sidecars. A regression to last-line/hex/default-0 parsing goes red.

Production _generate_execution_script output is rewritten onto a real host output dir and actually executed by cmd.exe (Windows) and bash (Linux) with a command emitting known tokens HELLO_OUT/HELLO_ERR (3) and LINUX_OUT/LINUX_ERR (5). Oracle = the real OS streams. Asserts the stdout token lands only in the .stdout sidecar, the stderr token only in .stderr, and the result file records the exact exit code (3/5). Broken 1>/2> redirection or echo %ERRORLEVEL%/$? goes red.
